title: Acoustic representations of different dimensions of the gendered self. An analysis of nonbinary and cisgender speakers
why_promising: Primary semi-spontaneous German production from 52 analyzed speakers. Recordings were manually segmented and annotated in Praat at picture, carrier-word and target-sound levels. The paper reports F0 characteristics, vowel formants/vowel-space measures, sibilant spectral properties, voice-quality measures and rich demographic/gender metadata, and states that dataset, Praat scripts and R code are available in an OSF repository.
open_question: Locate and verify the exact public OSF project URL and file-level access/license, then inventory and parse its token/acoustic tables. Do not admit to core until the public deposit is directly verified and lineage/deduplication can be checked.

title: The MRP Corpus: A Speech Dataset of Modern Received Pronunciation
why_promising: Primary contemporary British-English production corpus with more than 7,000 utterances from 29 speakers, word-level and phoneme-level transcripts, and a current 2026 methods paper. It could be valuable for timing, segmental, prosodic, and re-extracted acoustic measurements if its phone/word annotation workflow is sufficiently human-grounded.
open_question: Verify from the paper or annotation manual whether phoneme/word boundaries and labels were manually created, manually corrected, or exhaustively human-verified. The Zenodo metadata alone does not establish this; files are also restricted/request-access.

title: Dokumentation und Annotationsrichtlinien für das Korpus KGGS v3
why_promising: German read-speech corpus documentation provides an explicit annotation scheme and tier description for gender-neutral-language productions; potentially useful for segmental timing, prosody, realization variants, and future acoustic extraction.
open_question: Locate the underlying KGGS v3 corpus/data release, verify that the relevant temporal/phonetic tiers were manually created or exhaustively corrected rather than only automatically aligned, then check public file access and redistribution terms.

title: RescueSpeech: A German Corpus for Speech Recognition in Search and Rescue Domain
why_promising: Primary German production recorded during simulated search-and-rescue exercises, with approximately 3.7 GB of openly downloadable speech/enhancement data and repository documentation describing the recordings as manually annotated. This would add naturalistic/noisy speech outside laboratory tasks.
open_question: Determine exactly what 'manually annotated' means in the released ASR data: transcript/utterance labels only versus manually grounded word/phone intervals. Admit only the verified manual annotation layer and keep augmented speech-enhancement material separate from primary recordings.
